periods.analysis: We opened the series at 34 active Neighborhood Watch groups, above the target of 30 and in green status. That baseline reflects steady participation across the Harbor Heights, Bayfront, Old Mill, and East Dune sectors after the summer community-safety canvass. I am treating 34 not as a finish line, but as a documented operating level: active means the group has a named block captain, a current contact roster, and at least one logged meeting or patrol coordination during the quarter. Community trust is strongest when residents see the same process applied in every neighborhood.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 34-group base by completing a roster verification cycle for every active group before the next quarterly report. Extend the program by assigning Community Service Officers to the four highest-growth subdivisions and offering a standardized block-captain orientation at the October precinct open house. Keep the activation criteria unchanged so the count remains credible and comparable.

periods.analysis: The count moved from 34 to 33, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 1, while remaining green and above the target of 30. The reduction came after we consolidated two overlapping downtown waterfront groups that were using the same volunteer lead and reporting the same streets, so this is a quality-control adjustment rather than a loss of coverage. Holiday package-theft prevention kept participation steady, particularly on Routes NW-4 and SE-2 where patrol officers paired watch messaging with evening business checks. The important point is that we protected the integrity of the active-group definition while maintaining broad resident engagement.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the green result by completing post-consolidation contact updates for the affected waterfront blocks and confirming one accountable captain per group. Extend seasonal engagement by issuing the package-theft prevention bulletin through all 33 groups and tracking acknowledgments in the Community Trust log. Watch for volunteer fatigue in January and schedule two short virtual captain briefings instead of relying only on in-person meetings.

periods.analysis: Neighborhood Watch groups active declined from 33 to 31, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 2, but the measure remains green against the target of 30. This winter dip is not unexpected; two campus-adjacent groups paused activity during leadership turnover, and one retirement-community group shifted to a building-based safety committee that did not meet our active-watch criteria. We still have citywide coverage, but the margin above target narrowed to 1 group, which deserves careful attention. My assessment is that trust remains intact, provided we follow up plainly and do not count inactive structures for appearance's sake.
periods.recommendations: Sustain compliance by revalidating all 31 active groups through March sign-in sheets, captain confirmations, or patrol liaison notes. Extend capacity by recruiting replacement captains for the campus-adjacent blocks through the Harborview University safety office and the North Pier tenants association. Set a watch-item for any additional inactive group: if one more group drops, launch a 30-day reactivation plan with the district lieutenant assigned by sector.

periods.analysis: The count improved from 31 to 33, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 2, keeping the measure green and rebuilding the cushion above the 30-group target. The increase reflects two reactivations: the Cedar Lane student-rental corridor and the Seabreeze Villas retirement cluster, both of which completed captain training and submitted current contact lists. Spring events helped; officers used the Safe Streets Saturday booths to convert informal resident interest into documented watch participation. This is the right kind of growth because it restored known community nodes rather than creating paper groups.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 33 active groups by adding a mid-quarter check-in requirement for reactivated groups so they remain stable through summer travel. Extend the approach by bringing the same captain-training packet to the June homeowner association roundtable and the Marina District merchant breakfast. Keep the procedural standard visible: no group should be reported active without a roster, a captain, and a current communication channel.

periods.analysis: Neighborhood Watch groups active rose from 33 to 35, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 2, and the measure remains solidly green. Growth came from the new Breakwater Ridge subdivision and the South Harbor apartment cohort, where move-in orientations included a police liaison table and direct sign-up for block captains. Summer call-for-service briefings gave residents timely, factual information without overstating risk, which is important for trust. At 35 groups, Harborview has the strongest participation level in this eight-quarter run so far, and it is backed by documented engagement rather than informal interest.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 35-group level by assigning each new group a 90-day mentor captain from an established Harbor Heights or Bayfront watch. Extend the model to pending high-density permits on Compass Way by coordinating with Planning staff and property managers before occupancy. Continue monthly data snapshots for captains, limited to verified trends and prevention guidance, so engagement remains useful and measured.

periods.analysis: The count eased from 35 to 34, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 1, while staying green and comfortably above the target of 30. The decrease followed the planned merger of two small cul-de-sac groups in West Dune after their captains requested a shared schedule and common message thread. That change reduced administrative duplication without reducing neighborhood reach. We are ending the year with 34 active groups, which shows durable participation through the holidays and supports the broader trust objective.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 34 active groups by documenting the West Dune merger map and ensuring residents know which captain covers each street. Extend holiday-season effectiveness by pushing a single theft-prevention and vacation-watch checklist through every active group by the first week of December. Prepare a January leadership roster audit now, because orderly handoffs prevent small declines from becoming confidence issues.

periods.analysis: Neighborhood Watch groups active decreased from 34 to 32, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 2, but the measure remains green against the target of 30. The decline was tied to normal post-holiday attrition and two captain vacancies in the North Harbor rental corridor, not to a breakdown in resident willingness to participate. Still, the margin is again only 2 groups, so I am treating this as a watchful green result. We should be clear with the public: the program is healthy, but it depends on disciplined follow-through and named local leadership.
periods.recommendations: Sustain green status by completing captain succession calls for all 32 active groups and flagging any group without a backup lead. Extend recruitment in North Harbor by pairing the Community Engagement Unit with code-compliance outreach already scheduled for multifamily properties on Piermont Avenue. Set a concrete watch-item: fill the two captain vacancies or formally redraw those coverage areas before the end of April.

periods.analysis: The count increased from 32 to 34, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 2, returning the program to the same level seen in 2025-Q4 and keeping it green. The improvement came from reestablishing one North Harbor group under a new tenant captain and activating a new Compass Way watch after the first occupancy phase was completed. This closes the loop on the Q1 watch-item and shows that timely follow-up can recover participation without lowering standards. The overall arc is stable: Harborview has stayed above the 30-group target every quarter while improving the accuracy and accountability of the active roster.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 34 active groups by locking the updated roster into the quarterly Community Trust dashboard and confirming liaison assignments by patrol sector. Extend gains by offering the Compass Way onboarding template to the next two large residential developments before move-in permits are finalized. Continue reporting quarter-over-quarter movement plainly, because residents trust a program that is willing to show small declines and the corrective work behind the recovery.

periods.analysis: Active neighborhood watch groups rose from 34 to 35, above the target of 30.
periods.recommendations: Confirm captain and patrol-liaison assignments so the active roster continues to reflect groups residents can reach.
